newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner proposes end to staggered board.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner proposes end to staggered board.

text.p: Time Warner Inc said Thursday that its board will propose an end to its charter provisions requiring a classified board of directors.
In a release Wednesday the company said the board will vote on an amendment to Time Warner's certificate of incorporation eliminating such provisions.
The vote will take place at the 1997 annual meeting of stockholders, Time Warner said.
If adopted by the stockholders, the company said all directors would stand for election annually, beginning with the 1998 annual meeting of stockholders.

Time Warner Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gerald Levin said in the release that while the classified board "served the company well," it was no longer necessary, and shareholders should have a chance to vote on the entire board each year.
Levin also said in the release that the board unanimously voted for the elimination of the classified structure.
Levin said that the company has been on a "steady course toward enhancing governance procedures" through restructuring the board, by reducing the size and the number of insiders, for example.
